name: Soft Purple
lede: Soft Purple is an xkcd survey name where "soft" works as a general dulling modifier on a strong purple.

sections.title: A modifier, not a standard
sections.body:
Soft Purple comes from the xkcd 2010 color-name survey, where "soft" works as a general dulling modifier rather than naming a specific material [1]. The ISCC-NBS block for its region reads "strong purple", and in Munsell terms it sits near 6.1P 5.4/10.3, more saturated than the English word "soft" alone suggests [1].

Its closest cousins in our library are [[lavender|Lavender]] and [[orchid|Orchid]], both lighter purples [1]. The hex is a screen approximation; no dye or pigment is implied [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body:
No painting in our 23,781-painting archive carries this exact swatch covering at least 1% of its canvas, as photographed [2]. That describes the gap between this crowd-survey swatch and the purples our painting archive happens to hold, not a claim about painting as a whole [2].

In printed English, the phrase "soft purple" peaked in the 1870s and climbed fastest from the 1850s, well before the xkcd survey gave this exact hex its name in 2010, a reminder that the words and the swatch have separate histories [2].
